summary: Kathleen M. Higgins is a philosopher. She was a resident scholar at the Bellagio Center in 1993, a visiting fellow at the Australian National University in 1997, and Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2012).

Kathleen McDonald works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Lama Thubten Yeshe (~1974–1984), Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (~1974), and Tenzin Gyatso, Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche (all attested 2010).
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
Kathryn H. Selig Brown is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan by 2000 under the supervision of Walter M. Spink.

Katia Buffetrille specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Paris Nanterre University (~1986–1996) under Alexander W. Macdonald, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1998) and CRCAO.

Katragadda Paddayya is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his doctoral degree from Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1964–1968) and served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1970–2008).

Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras (1971–1973) under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught as an associate professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (1988–2003).
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (~1964–1969) and served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1999).

Katsuji Fujioka was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and Leipzig University (1901–1905). He served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held a post there from approximately 1901 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his MA under Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University and a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1972–1975), later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010).

Katsumi Okimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1973). He served as professor (~1982–2009) and director (~2009–2014) at Hanazono University.

Katsumi Tanabe is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1969) and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1993–2004) and Chuo University (~2004–2012).

Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist. He earned a doctorate from Kyoto University, worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture (~1931–1945) and Nara National Museum (1949–1967), and became a professor at Ryukoku University (~1965–1980).

Kavita Singh was an art historian and Indologist who earned her PhD from Panjab University (~1989–1996). She served as research editor at Marg Publications (~1999–2001) and became dean at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of Arts and Aesthetics in 2001.

Kazi Dawa Samdup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ugyen Gyatso and Lopen Tshampa Norbu. He served as headmaster of Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and became a lecturer at the University of Calcutta in 1920.

Kazu Uehara was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1992). He served as a full-time lecturer at the University of Miyazaki (~1957–1965) and later became professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1965–1995).

Kazuaki Komine is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Waseda University. He held positions at Tokushima University and the National Institute of Japanese Literature before becoming professor at Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as a scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and is a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor (attested 1982–1988) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013) at Shuchiin University.
